documents.title: Statement on Guidance for the University of Pennsylvania Community on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: Coders disagreed (A delegates, B permit). The statement opens "Penn embraces innovations like generative artificial intelligence" and sets conditions for everyone ("Disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool", verify output, protect data), with no ban or tiers. It says individual courses "may have different or more narrow guidance" and asks instructors for "clear guidelines", but that is a layer on top of a general welcome-with-conditions, so permit rather than delegates.
documents.summary: University-wide Penn guidance on generative AI from Information Systems and Computing. It sets principles (transparency, accountability, bias, privacy, security, IP) for all members, and gives separate short sections for educators, students and researchers. Students are told to follow course rules and otherwise treat AI like help from another person.

units.why: The opening sentence says "Penn embraces innovations like generative artificial intelligence" in teaching, learning and research, which is a university-wide default welcome of AI use (modality informs, phase general, actor all). It fits 'Permit or encourage AI by default' because the passage welcomes AI rather than setting up an institutional framework.
units.anchor: Penn embraces innovations like generative artificial intelligence (“AI”) models in teaching, learning, research
units.resolution_why: A coded P56 (institution-wide framework), B coded P02 (permit/encourage by default). The anchor itself says Penn "embraces" AI in teaching, learning and research; the framework is the rest of the document. A reader looking for the default welcome would look under P02, so P02 is final.
